title: ten proofs exec a bash script directly and Windows refuses it with WinError 193
intention: the ten proofs that exec bin/cairn or another bash script directly build that argv with bash_script_argv, so they run on Windows and are unchanged on POSIX.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: ten proofs raised OSError WinError 193 on a direct exec of a shebang script, read from the 2026-11-13 census rerun results.jsonl tails
traces_to: Law 3: the 193 was measured, and the fix is measured by rerunning each proof; Law 4: the scan is the physics that keeps the next proof from exec-ing a script bare.
how: At each site (cc test_superclaude_bare_box 83/89/91, clearance test_clearance_berths_in_codemother 277, codemother test_codemother_learning_lands_in_its_own_tables 276 and test_codemother_shows_an_artifact 63/72, librarian test_librarian_ask 269/273, operator test_the_operator_verbs_are_in_its_bin 148, recovery test_launchers_moved_to_their_devices 144, operator_inbox test_one_status_everywhere 80 and test_operator_inbox 300, tree test_tree_names_itself_the_one_tool 112) replace the bare script path at the head of the argv with *bash_script_argv(path), importing it from cairn.tools.base.script_argv. Red-first proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_no_proof_execs_a_bash_script_directly.py parses those ten files with ast and reds on any subprocess/_run argv headed by a bare script path and on a file that does not import bash_script_argv.

clauses.claim: the ast scan over the ten proofs finds no argv headed by a bare bin script path, where it found fourteen sites before the edit
each of the ten proofs imports bash_script_argv from cairn.tools.base.script_argv

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.how: grep of subprocess.run/_run call sites in the ten files
